summary.name: MockFlow
summary.one_liner: MockFlow is an online collaborative whiteboard for brainstorming, wireframing, prototyping and diagramming user interfaces and other visual work with a team.
use_cases: brainstorm ideas with a remote team
turn a web page into an editable wireframe
map system architecture and flows before building
build interactive classroom lessons with polls and quizzes
plan content calendars and campaign assets
summary.what_it_does: MockFlow provides a shared visual workspace where users sketch app and web screens with a widget library, restyle them, and wire them into clickable prototypes, with AI assistance. Clippy, its Chrome extension, sends any web page to the board as an editable wireframe. Auto layout keeps stacked widgets tidy, and stacks carry over to Figma. The board also supports architecture, ER, UML and sequence diagrams, mind maps, polls, timers, and audio or video meetings with comments. The page also describes Bridge, which connects local coding agents such as Claude Code to the board, and mini apps that teams can build and use together.
notable: Clippy Chrome extension turns any web page into an editable wireframe
AI-driven prototype generation and Mida assistant on the board
Auto layout with export to Figma
Bridge connects local coding agents like Claude Code and Codex to the board, with MCP connectors
caveats: Boards last 24 hours unless you sign up to keep them
Bridge is described as using your existing agent subscription, so it depends on that paid agent
Page says 'Free to start' but does not list specific paid tier prices
